Formal programme instruction is Dutch plus English while all 18 checked selected course offerings list Dutch.

routeSelection.basis: The normalized target is Pharmacy/Farmacie and the official current curriculum explicitly distinguishes the usual Farmacie study path from the separate Farmaceutische Wetenschappen path. The exact target-named Farmacie path is therefore reconstructed independently of UCR fit.

core: Molecular and cellular biology, biochemistry, human physiology, disease mechanisms and experimental investigation
Drug action, movement through the body, therapeutic use, toxicity, interactions and medicine safety
Laboratory, epidemiological, statistical and evidence-synthesis methods for medicine research and evaluation
adjacent: Quantitative modelling, data analysis and machine learning for drug action and treatment evidence
Safe medicine use, health behaviour, treatment decisions and the patient-facing role of pharmacy

alternatives.label: Molecular pharmacology, disease & medicine research
alternatives.concept: Study medicine action and safety through molecular and cellular biology, biochemistry, human physiology, pharmacology, anatomy, immunology, disease mechanisms, laboratory research, epidemiology and health behaviour. Preserve pharmaceutical chemistry, formulation, product-care and pharmacist-practice gaps explicitly.
alternatives.labelReason: The completed curriculum is dominated by molecular/physiological biology, pharmacology, disease, medicine safety and biomedical research, with health psychology and ethics as specific medicine-use complements; the label does not claim pharmacy practice.
progression: The schedule contains 24 unique courses / 180 EC, four courses per semester, PPD in Year 1 and seven level-300 courses. Every formal prerequisite occurs earlier and every course is available in its assigned Fall-2026-start term. Life/health foundations precede molecular biology, biochemistry, physiology, laboratory and advanced biomedical study; the brain-and-behaviour gateway precedes Medical & Health Psychology and the Advanced Research Seminar; Mathematical Methods precedes numerical methods and Probability & Statistics.

alternatives.label: Quantitative pharmacology & data-driven treatment
alternatives.concept: Retain molecular biology, physiology, pharmacology, disease mechanisms and laboratory research while prioritising mathematical systems, optimisation, machine learning and treatment-effect synthesis for quantitative study of drug action and therapeutic evidence.
alternatives.labelReason: Five anatomy, infection, health-psychology, ethics and neurobiology courses are replaced by advanced calculus, linear algebra, systems, optimisation and neural-network study, creating a quantitative drug-action curriculum without claiming pharmacometrics or pharmaceutical chemistry.
progression: The schedule contains 24 unique courses / 180 EC, four courses per semester, PPD in Year 1 and eight level-300 courses. Every formal prerequisite occurs earlier and every course is available in its assigned Fall-2026-start term. Biological and mathematical gateways precede all dependent work; biochemistry and physiology precede Pharmacology; introductory programming and data study precede advanced optimisation and neural-network implementation; biomedical statistics precedes systematic review and meta-analysis.
alternatives.distinctness: Five courses / 37.5 EC differ in each direction. Functional Anatomy, Infection & Immunity, Medical & Health Psychology, Ethics and Neurobiology are replaced by Advanced Calculus, Linear Algebra, Linear Systems, Optimization Methods in AI and Neural Networks & Deep Learning. The resulting choice shifts from biological systems, medicine use and patient context to quantitative modelling and data-driven treatment evidence.

candidates.label: Quantitative pharmacology, drug movement and treatment evidence

selection.assessment: Two complete related-field programmes pass the evidence, course-content, schedule and 30-EC distinctness gates. A third patient-facing pharmacy route is not defensible because the workbook lacks pharmaceutics and formulation, dispensing and product care, clinical pharmacy, medication review, dosage practice, patient counselling, pharmacy law/regulation and supervised pharmacist practice. General health psychology and ethics complement the first route but cannot be expanded into a pharmacy-practice curriculum.

Both involve experimental investigation; UCR supplies a broad life-science laboratory rather than medicine-specific pharmaceutical research.

notes.text: The UCR alternatives combine molecular and cellular biology, pharmacology, disease mechanisms, laboratory work, health behaviour and quantitative research. They do not reproduce pharmaceutical chemistry, formulation, product care, dispensing, clinical pharmacy, patient counselling, pharmacy regulation or supervised pharmacist practice, and therefore represent related biomedical routes rather than a full Pharmacy curriculum.
